root_cause.text: The mlx5e removal path in `drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_main.c` incorrectly performed PSP teardown in both `_mlx5e_remove()` and the NIC profile cleanup path `mlx5e_nic_cleanup()`, causing the same PSP object/refcount to be unregistered twice.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “PSP is unregistered twice in: `_mlx5e_remove -> mlx5e_psp_unregister` and `mlx5e_nic_cleanup -> mlx5e_psp_unregister`,” and the patch fixes it by deleting the direct `mlx5e_psp_unregister(priv);` call from `_mlx5e_remove()` because “the PSP cleanup happens as part of profile cleanup.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the explicit PSP unregister during registered-device removal to avoid incorrect teardown in this path and rely on netdev unregistration/suspend sequencing.
intent_record.what: The call to mlx5e_psp_unregister(priv); was removed from the NETREG_REGISTERED branch of _mlx5e_remove(), leaving unregister_netdev(priv->netdev); followed by _mlx5e_suspend(adev, false); unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, device removal no longer explicitly unregisters PSP in this code path before unregistering the netdevice, preventing that extra unregister action from occurring here and relying on the remaining teardown sequence instead.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the explicit PSP unregister during registered-device removal to avoid incorrect teardown in this path and rely on netdev unregistration/suspend sequencing.

relevance_review.reason: The change removes the explicit PSP unregister in the device removal path, which directly addresses the root cause of PSP teardown happening twice between _mlx5e_remove() and mlx5e_nic_cleanup().

candidates.rationale: This explicit PSP unregister in _mlx5e_remove() causes the PSP teardown to occur in this removal path even though NIC profile cleanup also unregisters it, leading directly to the double unregister/refcount bug.

vuln_statements.explanation: This explicit PSP teardown in _mlx5e_remove() duplicates the PSP unregister also performed via the NIC profile cleanup path mlx5e_nic_cleanup(), causing the same PSP object/refcount to be unregistered twice.
